prerequisites: A basic background in chemistry and biochemistry is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: knowledge of the main classes of biomaterials (metals, ceramics, polymers, and composite materials) and their structural characteristics
understanding of the relationship between the structure, properties, and performance of biomaterials
knowledge of the fundamental principles governing the interaction between biomaterials and the physiological environment, with particular emphasis on biocompatibility and biofunctionality
knowledge of the principal surface modification techniques and of the chemical, physical, mechanical, and biological methods used for biomaterial characterization
knowledge of the criteria for selecting biomaterials for major biomedical applications and the design of medical devices.
ability to correlate the structure, properties, and performance of biomaterials with specific biomedical applications
ability to critically evaluate the interactions between biomaterials and biological systems
ability to identify the most suitable biomaterial for a given application by considering functional, biological, and technological requirements
ability to interpret the results obtained from the main biomaterial characterization techniques
ability to apply the acquired knowledge to solve simple problems related to the design and development of biomedical devices.
ability to critically analyze the properties of biomaterials and their behavior in biological environments
ability to evaluate the advantages, limitations, and potential of different classes of biomaterials for specific clinical applications
ability to identify appropriate criteria for the selection and use of biomaterials in medical devices.
ability to describe the characteristics, properties, and applications of biomaterials using appropriate scientific language and technical terminology
ability to clearly and rigorously present the fundamental principles underlying the design, characterization, and application of biomaterials.
ability to use the acquired knowledge as a foundation for further learning in biomedical engineering, advanced biomaterials, and regenerative medicine
ability to independently deepen the topics covered in the course through the use of university-level textbooks and the relevant scientific literature.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to biomaterials and medical devices: History and evolution, definition and classification criteria (material/organism interaction, application, chemical nature), design principles.
Issues related to compatibility, reliability, and factors influencing the success of implants.

Properties of biomaterials: Analysis of biological properties (biocompatibility, toxicity), bulk properties (mechanical and viscoelastic), and surface properties, with an introduction to the main surface analysis techniques.
Tissue–biomaterial interactions: Study of the role of surface characteristics in the interaction with tissues and in biological response processes.
Classes of materials for biomedical applications: Metals, ceramics, and polymers: distinctive features and fields of application.
Examples of medical devices: Presentation of concrete case studies based on metallic, ceramic, and polymeric materials.

assessment_methods.method: Oral examination (follow-up questions, laboratory activities questions, general course topics questions)

assessment_rules: The assessment will be conducted through an oral examination. The examination includes a PowerPoint presentation of approximately 15 minutes, which constitutes 50% of the assessment. During the oral examination, follow-up questions will be asked to assess the student’s critical understanding of the selected topic. The discussion will also include questions related to the laboratory activities and general topics of the course. The final mark will be expressed on a thirty-point scale.
bibliography: Course slides and additional educational material will be made available by the teacher both in paper and digital form.
